titleStmt.title: Memorandum From Secretary of State Shultz to President Reagan

div.head: Memorandum From Secretary of State Shultz to President Reagan

list.label: SUBJECT
list.item: My Visit to Venezuela, Brazil and El Salvador

div.p: Venezuela’s sixth democratically elected president, Jaime Lusinchi, will be inaugurated between February 2 to 4. With your approval I would like to lead the delegation to the inauguration. As part of the same trip I would also hope to visit Brazil and El Salvador as planned in October.

The winner by a landslide, Lusinchi wants to establish a close working relationship with us. Under his leadership Venezuela will continue to stress the importance of democracy in Central America and in the Contadora process. Lusinchi also must tackle immediately the rescheduling of Venezuela’s $35 billion foreign debt and a severe economic downturn triggered by the fall in oil prices.

In Brazil, we will conclude our report on the five Working Groups which you and President Figueiredo created a year ago. Brazil wants and badly needs external support, both financial and symbolic. Its economy is severely constrained by its external imbalance and its political democratization has created a sense of uncertainty. The Brazilian government has been concerned that the US would not give sufficient importance to bilateral ties. Without a definitive show of external support, the country might not have sufficient self-confidence to resolve its economic problems in an orderly fashion and to conclude successfully its political democratization. While in Brazil, I also plan to meet with our Ambassadors in South America.

In El Salvador I will follow up George Bush’s successful visit last week with a full court press on the GOES to make and announce essential changes in several key areas that should strengthen our hand with the Congress. I also plan to review regional strategy at a meeting with our Ambassadors from the area.
I recommend you authorize me to lead the U.S. delegation to Venezuelan President-elect Lusinchi’s inauguration.
